news_drafts.headline: East Dunbartonshire health partnership depletes reserves to cover £4m shortfall and restricts service access
news_drafts.lead: East Dunbartonshire Health and Social Care Partnership used £8.2 million from its reserves to balance its 2026/27 budget but still forecasts an overspend of £4.1 million, according to budget monitoring reported this week. The partnership had set a savings target of £8.3 million but has achieved only £3.3 million to date. Staff pay awards of 3.5% and care home placements running 11 above approved numbers are driving costs. To manage the funding gap, the partnership has begun restricting access: service charges are rising, eligibility criteria are tightening, and waiting lists are extending. The partnership acknowledges that continued reliance on reserve drawdowns "may compromise" its sustainability and warns that demographic pressures will continue to drive costs while public funding remains constrained.

news_drafts.headline: East Dunbartonshire audit delays trigger formal investigation as material accounting errors emerge
news_drafts.lead: The Controller of Audit has launched a formal investigation into persistent delays at East Dunbartonshire Council in approving and publishing its annual accounts, with the expected timeline now slipping from August to October. The council's auditors, Forvis Mazars, identified significant risks in the council's financial management arrangements and discovered material errors in property accounting affecting £636 million of assets, including double-counted valuations of council dwellings. The auditors also unilaterally added £64,296 in fees to their bill without council approval. The council disputes responsibility for delays, claiming they "could have been avoided", but the findings—among them duplicate assets in the register and unapplied revaluations—prompted an explicit auditor recommendation for full reconciliation of the fixed asset register before next year's accounts.

news_drafts.headline: East Dunbartonshire health partnership faces £4m deficit and warns it cannot sustain further reserve depletion
news_drafts.lead: The Health and Social Care Partnership Integration Joint Board — a partnership between the council and NHS Greater Glasgow and Clyde — reported a projected overspend of £4.058m for 2026/27 at its meeting on 17 September. Of £8.324m in planned savings, the partnership has achieved only £3.274m to date. The gap stems largely from service reviews not yet completed due to staffing gaps, now being addressed. To publish a balanced budget, the partnership approved drawing £8.192m from its smoothing reserve — money set aside for emergencies. The board explicitly stated that continued reliance on reserves to cover recurring budget pressures "may compromise" the partnership's sustainability. General reserves will fall 68 per cent, from £3.955m to £1.290m. Care home placement numbers have also exceeded budget, now standing at 773 against an approved ceiling of 762, forcing restrictions on assessment practices.

findings.headline: The council holds no LOBO loans in its current portfolio, eliminating refinancing risk from lender call options.
findings.detail: The treasury portfolio as at 31 March 2026 and 31 July 2026 shows zero LOBO holdings. Total external borrowing comprises only Local Authorities (£35m and £72.5m), PWLB (£385.509m and £356.676m) and Market Loans (£6m and £5m), all of which are conventional fixed or variable rate instruments with known refinancing triggers.
findings.matters: LOBO loans carry lender refinancing risk; their absence simplifies the council's debt refinancing profile and removes a source of potential cost volatility.

findings.headline: The council's borrowing strategy is contingent on interest rates falling from current levels; if rates do not fall as forecast, the council will draw fixed-rate funding early at potentially higher cost.
findings.detail: The council is maintaining an under-borrowed position because it expects medium and longer-dated borrowing rates to fall. MUFG forecasts 5-year PWLB rates falling from 5.45% (August 2026) to 4.70% (June 2027). The Chief Finance Officer will adopt a pragmatic approach: postponing borrowing if rates look set to fall sharply, or drawing fixed-rate funding if rates threaten to rise more sharply than forecast.
findings.matters: Interest rate forecasts directly determine the timing and cost of material new borrowing over the next three years; material divergence from forecast could increase debt servicing costs significantly.
findings.figures: MUFG forecast: 5yr PWLB August 2026 5.45%, June 2027 4.70%; Bank Rate forecast at 3.75% through 2026/27
findings.quote: This strategy is prudent as medium and longer dated borrowing rates are expected to fall from their current levels, albeit only once prevailing inflation concerns are addressed by restrictive near-term monetary policy... The Chief Finance Officer will monitor interest rates in financial markets and adopt a pragmatic approach to changing circumstances

findings.headline: Under-borrowing position will converge from £27.565m to £1.684m over three years, meaning cash reserves will be largely exhausted to fund the capital programme.
findings.detail: The council is currently using cash balances to support part of its capital expenditure, maintaining an under-borrowed position where external debt trails the CFR. However, this position is forecast to narrow sharply, with under-borrowing reducing by 94% by 2028/29. Once under-borrowing converges, the council will need to fund all new capital expenditure through external borrowing.
findings.matters: Shows timing of when the council's cash reserves will be depleted and when it will become fully dependent on external markets for capital financing; critical for liquidity and refinancing planning.

findings.headline: The Capital Financing Requirement will grow from £565.180m to £785.457m over three years, an increase of £220.277m driven by capital spending plans.
findings.detail: The council's underlying borrowing need (the CFR) grows significantly from 2025/26 to 2028/29, increasing by 39% over the planning period. External borrowing grows correspondingly from £472.034m to £725.156m, with the largest year-on-year increase of £110.352m in 2027/28.
findings.matters: Indicates the scale of future external borrowing needs and the council's access to capital markets over the planning period; material for assessing debt trajectory and refinancing risk.
findings.figures: CFR: 2025/26 £565.180m, 2027/28 £748.566m, 2028/29 £785.457m; External borrowing forecast to grow from £472.034m to £725.156m

findings.headline: HRA capital expenditure forecast to reach £86.412m in 2027/28, more than five times the £15.963m spent in 2024/25.
findings.detail: The Housing Revenue Account capital programme is expanding sharply, from £15.963m (2024/25) through £42.889m (2026/27) to a peak of £86.412m (2027/28) before stepping back to £36.986m (2028/29). This represents a material commitment to housing investment, reflected in HRA borrowing growing from £68.237m to £225.488m over the same period.
findings.matters: Shows the council's scale of commitment to housing investment and determines future borrowing needs and debt servicing costs.
